subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should OpenClaw add Discord account/channel-level granular message gates for send, read, edit, and delete, or keep the coarse Discord `messages` gate and rely on generic message action allowlists for destructive controls?
rationale: This changes a public authorization/config contract and affects least-privilege semantics, account inheritance, generated metadata, docs, tests, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Add backward-compatible Discord granular gates
options.body: Preserve `messages: boolean` as shorthand while adding a documented granular shape that runtime and discovery both enforce.

options.title: Document generic allowlists only
options.body: Close the gap by documenting `tools.message.actions.allow` as the supported way to hide or block destructive message actions without changing Discord config.

options.title: Defer to cross-channel gate design
options.body: Keep this open or move it to a broader action-gate design so Discord does not get a one-off config shape.

recommendation.title: Add backward-compatible Discord granular gates
recommendation.body: Preserve `messages: boolean` as shorthand while adding a documented granular shape that runtime and discovery both enforce.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is a security/config contract choice, and the recent review and adjacent security/config history make this the best available routing owner.
